items.title: George "Tex" Stephens Interview, 1995-07-21
items.q: my cousin Lloyd Spencer... who used to promote Dave Bartholomew and all those guys over there.

ctx.x: Gee, I want to get back to something. Well, we've been showing this. You showed me this thing. It's about the reception. It's a brochure.

For William Taff, when you came to the president. President William Howard Taff. You said your grandfather was involved. Yeah, my grandfather was involved with that. What was his name? His name was Taylor, Lewis Taylor. He's not in here. I was looking for him, but this came out of his files. I got a hold of this some kind of way before he died, but he was a good friend with quite a few of these people who served on the executive committee, and they got him involved. That's, you know, because I talked with him,…

They died and the building was sold. Now, my cousin Lloyd Spencer, who at one time had Lloyd's Esquire Lounge, who used to promote Dave Bartholomew and all those guys over there. And incidentally, Lloyd is still alive today. I guess he could fill you in on a lot of people. He had Lloyd's Esquire Lounge over there in Gretna. And then another good friend, I guess I can say he's into my family because Merlin Dennis, who had the Peppermot Lounge in Gretna, he's married to my cousin. He's still alive, but he's kind of…

items.title: George "Tex" Stephens Interview, 1996-08-23
items.q: He was singing with Dave Bartholomew and his band. That's when I first met them on Ramport Street in the old studio where Casa Mombatassa made all the recordings years ago.

ctx.x: Did that cause the demise of that club? Because I don't think it...

I don't think so. No. No. I don't think it caused the demise of the club. I think things started changing with... You see, Club Desire was down in the Ninth Ward. But you had the Dewdrop, the Robin Hood, and all of these Johnny-come-lately clubs, which were just beginning to hit their stride to develop new entertainment. Then, like I said, you had the Coliseum Arena, which was in the central part of the city. You had the ILA Club, which was in the French Quarter. You had all of these things jumping against…
How do you see the difference? Is there any difference between rhythm and blues and rock and roll? I mean, did you see a difference?

items.title: George "Tex" Stephens Interview, 1996-01-10
items.q: Until all of a sudden, Dave Bartholomew, who had one of the biggest bands in the city of New Orleans, a young man who had just gotten out of the service and started...

ctx.x: Okay, so why don't we try to, okay, we're back with Tech Stevens, January 10th, 1996, reel number one. Okay. Yeah, let's try to get the microphones closer and you know how that stuff goes. Wait, so we're talking about, we're talking about advertising and stuff, that's okay, just advertising, not advertising, we're talking about, you brought up the Dawn Patrol, why don't you continue on who was the Dawn Patrol and what it was? Well, the Dawn Patrol was started

by the Pittsburgh Courier in order to enhance the musical structure in and around the greater metropolitan area of New Orleans that everything would start around about midnight. And for all of the bands who probably played at the French Quarter, or maybe some of the other clubs in and around the city, if you go on, like Club Desire, like the Robin Hood, maybe some who played just any place, maybe the Lloyd's at Square Lounge on the West Bank of the River, or maybe on Jesse's over in Marrero, or maybe at Louis…
All righty. You know, Ted, I think it's about time that we start talking about a young man who had one of the greatest radio trademarks ever in history.
